chapter_name: A Pair of Mustachios (by Mulk Raj Anand)
learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the foolishness of false pride and rigid class distinctions through a hilarious satire about a man who sells his entire livelihood over a mustache!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The story introduces a strict social code where the style of one's mustache dictates their social class. A 'lion' mustache is for royalty, a 'tiger' for feudal lords, and a flat 'goat' mustache is for commoners and moneylenders.

Azam Khan claims royal Afghan descent but is actually poor. When he sees Seth Ramanand (a humble grocer and moneylender) wearing a 'tiger' mustache with the tips turned up, he takes it as a massive personal insult.

To make Ramanand lower the tips of his mustache to a 'goat' style, Azam Khan foolishly signs away all his property and lands to the clever moneylender. He loses everything just to satisfy his hollow ego.

fun_activity.title: 🧔 Design the Mustachios
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a face and try sketching the different mustaches described in the story: the proud Lion, the fierce Tiger, and the humble Goat. See how changing just the facial hair changes the whole 'attitude' of the drawing!

exam_tips: 📌 Satire: This story is a perfect example of satire. Anand mocks the feudal mindset and the absurdity of clinging to past glory when one has no present wealth.
📌 Ramanand's Cunningness: Contrast Azam's hot-headed foolishness with Ramanand's cool, calculating nature. Ramanand sacrifices a bit of mustache-pride to gain actual wealth.
📌 The mustache acts as a powerful symbol of caste, class, and male ego in colonial Indian society.
quick_recap: ⭐ In this society, mustache styles are strictly tied to caste and class.
⭐ Impoverished aristocrat Azam Khan gets enraged at a grocer for wearing his mustache tips up.
⭐ Azam sells all his property to the grocer just to force him to turn the tips down, ruining himself for false pride.
